en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Loch Arbour, Monmouth County, New Jersey, 1905, Sheet 7

properties.name: Elberon Avenue / Norwood Avenue / Norwood Avenue South

sheet-9999997.description: This sheet, numbered 7 and headed Loch Arbour, covers the whole of the small seaside settlement of Loch Arbour on the strip of land between Deal Lake and the Atlantic Ocean, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the right of the page. Deal Lake runs down the left side of the sheet, and an iron bridge at the upper left carries Norwood (Main) Avenue across it towards Asbury Park. Norwood (Main) Avenue forms the inland edge of the sheet along the top; Edgmont Avenue follows the curving lake shore, and Euclid Avenue and Elberon Avenue run down the sheet to the beach. Lake Avenue (Ocean Road) crosses the middle of the sheet, and Ocean Avenue runs parallel to it a block from the shore. The blocks are divided into numbered lots, most of them still vacant; the buildings shown are mostly frame dwellings of one and a half to three stories, several with open porches and private stables. The largest building is The Throck Morton, a three-and-a-half-storey frame building at Norwood Avenue near the lake, noted as heated by furnace and lit by gas and electricity, with a cottage beside it. Near the mouth of the lake at the lower left stand the U.S. Life Saving Station No. 6, a row of bathing houses with an office and a pavilion. The beach lots between Ocean Avenue and the shore are drawn empty. Four-inch water pipes, some dated 1898, run in the streets, with hydrants marked at the corners. Neighbouring sheets 6 and 8 are referenced at the top and right edges, and block key numbers 1 to 6 and 10 are printed in the blocks.
notes: Norwood (Main) Avenue is now Norwood Avenue (Norwood Avenue South at its south end); modern Main Street (Route 71) is further inland.
Lake Avenue (Ocean Road) is now Ocean Avenue South; Ocean Avenue is now Ocean Place.
Edgmont Avenue is now Edgemont Drive, and its stretch to the beach Edgemont Avenue.
The Throck Morton is the largest building on the sheet; U.S. Life Saving Station No. 6 stands near the mouth of Deal Lake.
Scale 60 ft to an inch, an unusual scale for the series.
The canvas is labelled 9999997 in the manifest; the printed sheet number is 7 (N.J.C.M. vol. 2).

Printed sheet 7 of N.J.C.M. vol. 2 (canvas label 9999997). One part, scale 60 ft to an inch, north to the right. Loch Arbour between Deal Lake and the Atlantic: Norwood (Main) Av (now Norwood Avenue), Edgmont Av, Euclid Av, Elberon Av, Lake Av (Ocean Road) (now Ocean Avenue South), Ocean Av (now Ocean Place); U.S. Life Saving Station No. 6, bathing houses, The Throck Morton.
